This is huge news not only in and of itself, but also politically.

For those not following the current space game going on. During the Bush era NASA began work on the so called Constellation Program. This program had a viable timeline and budget for NASA to go from nothing to Mars while using the moon as an in-between stepping stone. Shortly after coming into office Obama decided to scrap this program, citing costs, and instead directed NASA to begin development of the Space Launch System(SLS).

The SLS is essentially the Space Shuttle 2.0. It's based on modestly incremental technology over what we had in the 60s. It's also an enormously expensive pork project. The aim is for half a billion dollars per launch and that's before development costs which are expected to hit the tens of billions. It's being developed by Boeing and Lockheed whom for decades have been taking advantage of uncompetitive government contracts. The $1.5 trillion under performing jet fighter, the F-35, is a product of Lockheed.

Now enter Trump. Trump has been cutting government expenditures and Lockheed/Boeing have already come up numerous times. In relations to costs with the F-35 as well as the planned updates to Air Force 1 (which was going to be more than $4 billion for a single plane). He's also set his sights on the SLS. SLS development began in 2011. Its first planned flight is for 2018 which was supposed to be an unmanned circumnavigation of the moon. For context Kennedy's space speech was in 1962. 7 years later from that time we had men on the moon. Recently Trump formally inquired as to the feasibility of their upgrading the flight to a manned circumnavigation.

I don't think that inquiry was happenstance. I believe that Trump, who has been directing more funds into space exploration and human projects, is giving Boeing/Lockheed a soft warning and an opportunity to justify their costs. NASA has responded to this inquiry in a less than particularly ambitious fashion. However, if SpaceX achieves this launch in 2018, privately - and certainly for a tiny fraction of what SLS is charging - I think it's likely that will signal the end of the SLS program, ideally with a greater boost towards commercial space providers such as SpaceX. Boeing and Lockheed are not going to take this lying down.

So I think we're looking at the beginning of what is going to be, even if on just an intranational scale (for now), the Space Race 2.0. Expect to see the SLS suddenly kick into gear. They're going to do everything they can to get that mission manned - and do it before SpaceX.
